## Summary

Implemented server-assigned `customerCode` formatted `<LAST3>-<NNNN>` on owner creation.

**What the format means (per spec & test):** LAST3 = upper-cased first three letters of `lastName`; NNNN = 4-digit zero-padded global sequence equal to *one more than the current number of owners*. Computed before the new owner is saved, so two successive creates get consecutive numbers (`SMI-000N`, then `JON-000N+1`), which is exactly what `Cp09Tests.coreFormatAndGlobalSequence` asserts.

**Changes:**
- `model/Owner.java` — added `customerCode` field (`@Column(name="customer_code")`) with getter/setter.
- `rest/function/owner/AssignCustomerCode.java` (new) — reads the built `Owner` via `@Val`, counts owners via `OwnerRepository.findAll().size() + 1`, and sets `String.format("%s-%04d", last3, sequence)`. Guards short surnames with `Math.min(3, length)`.
- `officefloor/rest/api/owners.POST.yml` — inserted an `assignCustomerCode` step between `build` and `save`, under the same `transaction` governance (so the count sees the seed data plus prior commits, but not the not-yet-saved current owner).
- `openapi.yml` — added `customerCode` as a `readOnly` property on the `Owner` response schema (drives the generated `OwnerDto`; MapStruct auto-maps it by name, so the value flows out on `GET /api/owners/{id}`).
- DB schemas (`hsqldb`, `h2`, `postgres`, `mysql`) — added a `customer_code` column; and the positional seed inserts in `hsqldb`/`mysql` `data.sql` got a trailing `NULL` to match the new column count (h2/postgres use named-column inserts, so they were unaffected).

Tests use the `hsqldb` profile; the initial `row column count mismatch` was the positional seed inserts, now fixed.
